content.title: About
content.content: Chicken quesadilla is a Mexican dish consisting of a thin wheat or corn tortilla filled with shredded chicken, melted cheese, and sometimes vegetables, then toasted until golden. The result is a tender bite of seasoned chicken, stretchy cheese, and a lightly crisp exterior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word “quesadilla” comes from the Spanish “queso,” meaning “cheese.”
Traditional Mexican quesadillas are made with corn tortillas, while U.S. versions often use flour tortillas.
Chicken is usually grilled or cooked in a chili‑based sauce, giving the filling a distinctive flavor.
Quesadillas are commonly served with salsa, guacamole, and sour cream.
The dish gained fast‑food popularity because it is quick to assemble and easy to eat on the go.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Cheese adds calcium, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both chicken and cheese supply B6 and B12 vitamins, important for nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Low in simple carbs
items.content: When made with whole‑grain tortillas, the dish has fewer simple carbohydrates, helping blood‑sugar control.

items.title: Micronutrients
items.content: Iron, zinc, and magnesium are present, contributing to immune support and energy production.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauces and cheese often contain a lot of salt; those with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The combination of cheese and oil makes quesadillas calorie‑rich, so moderation is advised.

items.title: Food‑borne bacteria
items.content: Chicken must be cooked thoroughly to prevent salmonella risk.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cut the quesadilla into wedges and serve hot. It can be enjoyed alone or with salsa, guacamole, sour cream, and fresh vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in a skillet or oven to restore crispness.
